rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reading burden for verification = banned. Claude audits Claude.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 25 (raw source) IS a manual-read-for-error instruction: "If twenty minutes in you can see Claude hallucinating file paths, contradicting its own earlier steps, or missing a requirement that wasn't in the prompt, stop it." That names exactly the correctness-error class \u00a7 30 targets, so this is not a clean absence. It survives on the rule's own carve-out: "M5/M6 teach Claude-on-Claude verification; earlier modules foreshadow, not pre-empt." This lecture sets up M4, whose deliberate design (backing claim `un-packaged-first-by-design`, "no plan.md, no verifier, no reference artifact") is that session one has no automated verifier — the student's own read IS the mechanism, by design, and M5 is where a verifier is added as one of the packaging pieces ("watch each packaging piece close a specific gap you just saw"). The maintainer watch-for confirms the intent directly: "Frame it as the read is the deliverable, not what nervous students can fall back on." Foreshadowing, not pre-emption — stays inside the exception.
